method_card.title: Identity and Self-Description
method_card.content:
This lesson covers who you are: your nationality, the languages you speak, your values and how you introduce yourself. The central grammar point is ser + adjective for identity, with careful attention to lowercase nationalities and adjective agreement.

SpanishEnglish
soy inglés / soy inglesaI am English (m/f)
español / españolaSpanish (m/f)
francés / francesaFrench (m/f)
alemán / alemanaGerman (m/f)
galés / galesaWelsh (m/f)
irlandés / irlandesaIrish (m/f)
hablo español / inglés / francésI speak Spanish / English / French
soy bilingüeI am bilingual
los valoresvalues
la identidadidentity
me llamomy name is
tengo … añosI am … years old
provengo deI come from (Higher)
las raícesroots / origins (Higher)

Grammar focus: nationalities are NOT capitalised in Spanish. This is a critical Spanish-specific rule. Write soy inglés, NOT soy Inglés. Write hablo español, NOT hablo Español. Only the country name takes a capital: España, Francia, Alemania, Gales.

Nationality adjectives agree for gender: inglés (m) / inglesa (f). Nationalities ending in a consonant add -a for feminine. Use ser for nationality (permanent identity): Soy inglés. Never estoy inglés.

Model paragraph: Me llamo Pablo, tengo dieciséis años y soy inglés. Mis padres son de España, así que hablo español e inglés. En mi opinión, ser bilingüe es una ventaja enorme. (My name is Pablo, I am sixteen and I am English. My parents are from Spain, so I speak Spanish and English. In my opinion, being bilingual is a huge advantage.)
steps: Learn nationality vocabulary — always lowercase in Spanish
Master ser + nationality adjective with correct gender agreement
Practise saying which languages you speak
Build a self-introduction using tengo años, soy, hablo and opinion phrases

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — introducing yourself and nationalities appear every year

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: Me llamo Sofía, tengo quince años y soy española.

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Me llamo Sofía = My name is Sofía. tengo quince años = I am fifteen (literally: I have fifteen years).

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: soy española = I am Spanish. Note: española is lowercase in Spanish and agrees with the feminine subject.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: My name is Sofía, I am fifteen years old and I am Spanish.

worked_examples.question: Spot the error: Me llamo Diego, tengo dieciséis años y soy Inglés.

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Check each element: me llamo ✓, tengo dieciséis años ✓, soy ✓ (ser for nationality).

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Inglés has a capital letter. In Spanish, nationalities are NEVER capitalised — only country names are.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: The error is Inglés — it should be inglés (lowercase). Spanish nationalities are never capitalised.

bronze.question: Match the nationality to its English meaning
Match the Spanish to the English meaning

gaps.correct_explain: Me llamo = My name is (literally: I call myself). The reflexive pronoun is me.

wrong.Mi: Mi llamo is wrong. Mi is a possessive (my). The correct reflexive construction is Me llamo.

gaps.correct_explain: tengo is the yo form of tener. In Spanish, age is expressed with tener: tengo dieciséis años.

wrong.tienen: tienen is the ellos/ellas form (they have). The subject is 'I' → tengo.

gaps.correct_explain: soy is the yo form of ser. Always use ser for nationality.

wrong.estoy: estoy is from estar, used for temporary states and location. Nationality is a permanent identity → soy.

gaps.correct_explain: son is the plural of ser. Use ser + de for origin: mis padres son de España.

wrong.están: están de España is wrong. Estar is for location (where you are now). Ser de = to be from (origin).

gaps.correct_explain: española agrees with the feminine noun madre. Note: nationalities are always lowercase in Spanish.

wrong.espanola: Missing accent: the correct spelling is española. The tilde over the ñ is essential.

gaps.correct_explain: español agrees with the masculine noun padre. Always lowercase.

wrong.espanol: Missing accent: the correct spelling is español. The accent on the o is essential.

bronze.question: Which sentence correctly says 'My name is Lucía, I am fifteen and I am Irish'?
options: Me llamo Lucía, tengo quince años y soy irlandesa.
Me llamo Lucía, tengo quince años y soy Irlandesa.
Me llamo Lucía, estoy quince años y soy irlandesa.
Me llamo Lucía, tengo quince años y estoy irlandesa.

bronze.question: What does 'Hablo inglés, francés y un poco de español' mean?
options: I speak English, French and a bit of Spanish
I speak English, French and a lot of Spanish
I spoke English, French and a bit of Spanish
I will speak English, French and Spanish

bronze.source_text: Soy galés y hablo galés e inglés. Creo que hablar dos idiomas es muy útil.
model_answers: I am Welsh and I speak Welsh and English. I think that speaking two languages is very useful.

silver.question: Complete the sentence
silver.english: My parents are Spanish and I am British, so I consider myself bilingual.

gaps.correct_explain: españoles agrees with padres (masculine plural). Note: lowercase, and the accent on é is retained in the plural.

wrong.española: española is feminine singular. Padres is masculine plural → españoles.

gaps.correct_explain: soy is the yo form of ser. Use ser for permanent identity and nationality.

wrong.estoy: estoy is from estar. Nationality is a permanent identity → soy, not estoy.

gaps.rule: Adjective ending in -e — no gender change
gaps.correct_explain: bilingüe ends in -e so it does not change for gender. Note the ü (u with diaeresis) is required — without it, the g before e would sound like a Spanish j.

wrong.bilinguo: bilinguo does not exist. The correct form is bilingüe — the diaeresis on the ü makes the u audible.
wrong.bilingues: bilingues would be the plural. The subject here is singular (yo) → bilingüe.

silver.question: Find and fix the grammatical error
silver.sentence: Me llamo Hugo, estoy alemán y hablo alemán e inglés.
silver.explanation: Nationality is a permanent identity. Use ser (→ soy), not estar (→ estoy). Estoy is for temporary states and locations.
silver.translation: My name is Hugo, I am German and I speak German and English.

silver.question: Build the sentence in Spanish
silver.english: In my opinion, speaking two languages is a huge advantage.

distractor_labels.gran: gran shortens from grande before a singular noun — but here enorme is the better word and gran would need to be placed before ventaja. Both are possible; the model uses enorme after the noun.

silver.source_text: My name is Mateo. I am sixteen years old and I am Spanish. I speak Spanish and a little French.
model_answers: Me llamo Mateo. Tengo dieciséis años y soy español. Hablo español y un poco de francés.
hints: I am ... years old = tengo ... años

gold.source_text: My name is Lucía and I am seventeen years old. I am Welsh but my parents are from Spain, so I consider myself bilingual. In my opinion, having mixed roots is a real advantage.
model_answers: Me llamo Lucía y tengo diecisiete años. Soy galesa pero mis padres son de España, por eso me considero bilingüe. En mi opinión, tener raíces mixtas es una ventaja de verdad.

gold.question: Build the sentence in Spanish
gold.english: I am English but I speak Spanish because my mother is from Spain.

distractor_labels.Estoy: wrong verb — use ser (soy) for nationality, not estar (estoy)
distractor_labels.Español: wrong capitalisation — nationalities are lowercase in Spanish: español not Español
distractor_labels.francesa: wrong nationality — the mother is from Spain (española / de España), not France

gold.question: Role Play
gold.scenario: You are at a tourist information office in a Spanish-speaking city. A member of staff asks you about yourself. Answer in Spanish.

bullets.prompt: Introduce yourself: your name, age and nationality.
bullets.model_answer: Me llamo Daniel, tengo dieciséis años y soy inglés.
bullets.note: me llamo + tengo ... años + soy + nationality (lowercase)

bullets.prompt: Say which languages you speak and why you speak them.
bullets.model_answer: Hablo inglés y español porque mi madre es española y mis abuelos viven en España.

bullets.prompt: Ask for a map of the city and say where you are from.
bullets.model_answer: ¿Tiene un mapa de la ciudad, por favor? Soy de Londres.

bullets.prompt: Give your opinion on visiting Spanish-speaking countries.
bullets.model_answer: En mi opinión, visitar países hispanohablantes es una experiencia increíble porque aprendo mucho.
bullets.note: en mi opinión + infinitive as subject + reason

gold.question: Listen and type what you hear
gold.audio_text: Me llamo Sofía, soy española pero vivo en Inglaterra. Hablo español e inglés con fluidez.
gold.correct_text: Me llamo Sofía, soy española pero vivo en Inglaterra. Hablo español e inglés con fluidez.
gold.translation: My name is Sofía, I am Spanish but I live in England. I speak Spanish and English fluently.

gold.question: Complete the sentence
gold.english: I think that having roots in two countries makes you richer as a person, although it can sometimes be difficult.
sentence_parts: Creo que tener raíces en dos países te hace más

gaps.rule: Adjective agreement — te refers to the speaker
gaps.correct_explain: rico agrees with a masculine speaker (or rica for feminine). The adjective describes te (you), so it agrees with the person speaking.

wrong.ricos: ricos is plural. The subject is a single person → rico (masculine) or rica (feminine).
wrong.ricas: ricas is feminine plural. The subject is a single person → rico or rica.

gaps.correct_explain: pueda ser uses the subjunctive of poder (pueda) because aunque + subjunctive signals a hypothetical or concessive meaning ('even if it might be'). Alternatively sea (subjunctive of ser) also works.

wrong.puede ser: puede ser (indicative) after aunque treats the difficulty as a stated fact. Using the subjunctive (pueda ser) is preferred in Higher tier writing to indicate that you are acknowledging a possibility rather than a certainty.
wrong.es: es is the present indicative. After aunque for a concession expressing uncertainty, the subjunctive is preferred at Higher tier.
